text: 🇲🇽🏫 One high school, two certificates: general + technical, backed by a public university. Texcoco's new agro-tech campus starts its second construction phase this year: dairy, poultry and pork production units. It is part of the Plan Integral for the eastern State of Mexico — 10 municipalities, 10 million residents, each getting at least one new preparatoria or a public university campus (UNRC or UBBJ). — Comunicado, Presidencia de la República

🇲🇽🎓 "We are going to at least double the goal — 400,000 new high school places across the country." "Today it's 200,000 more places nationwide, and very soon we will announce that demand for the preparatorias has been so high that we are going to at least double the goal. It will be at least 400,000 places for upper-secondary education during this administration." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum Pardo, Texcoco, State of Mexico Sheinbaum inaugurated a Bachillerato Tecnológico Agropecuario in Texcoco — 50 million pesos, 12 classrooms, 1,080 students across two shifts.

🇲🇽🐖 <u>MEXICO IS NOW THE WORLD'S TOP PORK IMPORTER — A FOOD-SOVEREIGNTY WARNING</u>

Mexico just passed Japan as the world's biggest buyer of foreign pork: 1.6 million tons imported in 2025, up 8.8% year on year, against domestic production of 1.365 million tons, per El Economista. Total consumption hit 2.775 million tons — most of the pork Mexicans eat now crosses a border, mainly from the US. The same country that lectures Mexico about trade deficits feeds its table. Food sovereignty remains the unfinished business.

🇲🇽🛡️ <u>HALF OF MEXICO'S HOMICIDES HAPPEN IN JUST 60 MUNICIPALITIES — THAT'S WHERE THE STRATEGY AIMS</u>

The map of violence is not the whole country: around half of all homicides are concentrated in 60 priority municipalities, and that is exactly where the National Security Strategy concentrates operations and social programs, per the SSPC. The results keep compounding — 2025 closed with an 18% drop in the homicide rate. Precision over militarized scattershot.

🇲🇽🌲 <u>MEXICO SEIZES 1,451 CUBIC METERS OF ILLEGALLY LOGGED TIMBER IN FOUR DAYS</u>

Profepa hit illegal loggers hard this week: 1,451.3 cubic meters of timber and forest raw materials seized between August 3 and 6 in operations against illegal logging and its black-market trade. One front of a wider strategy — fire brigades deployed across the country and a national reforestation drive. Environmental policy with boots on, not press releases.

🇲🇽🥬 <u>ANOTHER US "OUTBREAK" PINNED ON MEXICAN PRODUCE FALLS APART</u>

Washington flagged Mexican lettuce as a possible source of cyclospora cases in the US. Mexico ran the tests: lettuce from Guanajuato came back negative for the parasite, and Health Secretary David Kershenobich confirmed only 33 cases nationwide through July 31 — a low figure for 130 million people. Last time the FDA cried outbreak over Mexican greens, it was a false positive. The pattern is the policy.

🇲🇽🇨🇺 <u>"THE ISLAND WILL NOT SURRENDER": CUBA'S EMBASSY IN MEXICO MARKS FIDEL'S CENTENARY</u>

At the Mexico presentation of "Fidel: 17 aproximaciones," coordinated by John Saxe-Fernández, Cuba's second chief of mission Johana Tablada put it plainly: "Though it hurts imperialism, the Cuban people still follow the example of resistance and rebellion marked by Fidel Castro." Blackouts of over 20 hours, shortages of water and medicine — a US blockade built to collapse the island. A century after Fidel's birth, Havana's answer is the same: no se rinde.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>MEXICO'S TAX AUTHORITY TURNS ON ITS OWN: 74 OFFICIALS REPORTED TO PROSECUTORS</u>

The cleanup starts at home. Mexico's SAT has denounced 74 of its own officials before the FGR so far this year — the highest figure in two decades. Hacienda's breakdown: 34 for illicit access to the agency's own computer systems, 28 for abuse of their powers. While the old guard screams "persecution," the 4T is auditing the people who collect the taxes.
